Delete volume, pool or job.

## Synopsis

```text
delete [yes] [catalog=<catalog>]
delete volume[=<volume>] [yes] [catalog=<catalog>] [pool=<pool>]
delete pool[=<pool>] [yes] [catalog=<catalog>]
delete jobid=<jobid>[,...] [yes] [catalog=<catalog>]
delete storage[=<storage>] [yes] [catalog=<catalog>]
```

Words without brackets are required, `[ ]` marks optional parts, `a | b` alternatives, `...` a repeatable argument and `[,...]` a comma separated list.

## Description

Deletes catalog records of volumes, pools, jobs or storages; asks unless yes is given.

## Arguments {#arguments}

| Argument | Type | Values / source | Default | Flags | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `yes` | keyword |  |  |  | Do not ask. |
| `catalog=` | resource | from [`.catalogs`](../dot-catalogs/) |  |  | Catalog name. |

These arguments apply to every subcommand as well.

## Subcommands

### delete volume {#sub-delete-volume}

**A volume record.**

Deletes a volume and every job stored on it from the catalog. The data on the medium is untouched, but it can no longer be selected for restore. Without a name the pool and volume are selected in a dialogue; pool= sets the pool for this selection. The Director asks for confirmation unless yes is given; the action cannot be undone.

Onesimus deviation: a volume holding jobs of the latest Full chain of a client and FileSet is never deleted, not even with yes.

```text
delete volume[=<volume>] [yes] [catalog=<catalog>] [pool=<pool>]
```

| Argument | Type | Values / source | Default | Flags | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `volume=` | resource | from [`.media`](../dot-media/) |  | value optional | Volume name. |
| `pool=` | resource | from [`.pools`](../dot-pools/) |  |  | Pool of the volumes to select. |

Also accepts the arguments of [delete](#arguments): `yes`, `catalog`.

Delete a volume without asking:

```text
delete volume=Full-0001 yes
```

Choose the volume to delete from pool Scratch:

```text
delete volume pool=Scratch
```

### delete pool {#sub-delete-pool}

**A pool record.**

Deletes a Pool record from the catalog after confirmation; without a name the pool is chosen from a list. Onesimus deviation: deleting pools is not implemented yet, and after yes the Director answers delete pool: not supported.

```text
delete pool[=<pool>] [yes] [catalog=<catalog>]
```

| Argument | Type | Values / source | Default | Flags | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pool=` | resource | from [`.pools`](../dot-pools/) |  | value optional | Pool name. |

Also accepts the arguments of [delete](#arguments): `yes`, `catalog`.

Ask to delete the Scratch pool record:

```text
delete pool=Scratch
```

### delete jobid {#sub-delete-jobid}

**Job records (list or ranges).**

Deletes jobs together with their file and JobMedia records from the catalog. The value may be a comma-separated list with ranges such as 507-509,511; a range of more than 25 JobIds requires confirmation. Without a value the Director asks for the JobId. This is also the way to remove a single job of a protected latest Full chain.

```text
delete jobid=<jobid>[,...] [yes] [catalog=<catalog>]
```

| Argument | Type | Values / source | Default | Flags | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jobid=` | string |  |  | list | Job IDs. |

Also accepts the arguments of [delete](#arguments): `yes`, `catalog`.

Delete one job record:

```text
delete jobid=14
```

Delete two job records:

```text
delete jobid=600,602
```

### delete storage {#sub-delete-storage}

**A storage record.**

Deletes an orphaned Storage record from the catalog, one that no longer exists in the configuration. A storage still configured is refused; remove it from the configuration first. Without a value the Director asks for the name.

```text
delete storage[=<storage>] [yes] [catalog=<catalog>]
```

| Argument | Type | Values / source | Default | Flags | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `storage=` | resource | from [`.storages`](../dot-storage/) |  | value optional | Storage name. |
| `storage=` | resource | from [`.storages`](../dot-storage/) |  |  | Storage name. |

Also accepts the arguments of [delete](#arguments): `yes`, `catalog`.

Remove the catalog record of a removed storage:

```text
delete storage=OldTape
```

## Examples

Choose what to delete from the menu:

```text
delete
```

Delete four job records:

```text
delete jobid=507-509,511
```
